text:
John L. Pollock, born John Leslie Pollock in 1940, was a philosopher who studied physics, mathematics, and philosophy, earning a triple-major degree from the University of Minnesota in 1961. His doctoral dissertation from the University of California, Berkeley, advised by Ernest Adams, included an appendix on defeasible reasoning which became a key part of his later philosophical contributions. He held faculty positions at several universities, including the University of Arizona, where he helped establish the Cognitive Science Program.
Pollock gained recognition for his work in epistemology, notably with his book *Knowledge and Justification* (1974). His philosophical work was heavily centered on defeasible reasoning, leading to him being known as "Mr. Defeasible Reasoning." Key concepts from his work include "undercutting defeat" and "rebutting defeat," and he also developed the software prototype OSCAR, which implemented his ideas on defeasible reasoning alongside concepts of intentions, interests, and cognitive architectural design. He was also a contributor to the 1990 publication *Nomic Probability and the Foundations of Induction* .
